sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface localization confirmed by design (heterologous SP drives surface targeting); ortholog HA-tagged mouse Mer confirmed on cell surface by live-cell labeling (non-permeabilized staining, PMC4206827). Receptor function not explicitly assayed for the FLAG-tagged construct.
sites.rationale: L1 explicitly states the FLAG tag is placed between the signal peptide and the Mertk mature peptide sequence in a full-length, membrane-anchored construct, which in UniProt canonical numbering corresponds to insert_after_residue=20 (last residue of the signal peptide, R) and residue_after=21 (A, first residue of the mature extracellular domain). Python-verified: residue 20 = R, residue 21 = A, and the mature N-terminus is 481 residues from the TM boundary, well exceeding the ≥3-residue clearance requirement. L3/L4 (PMC4206827) independently show that HA-tagged mouse Mer (ortholog) is surface-displayed by live-cell labeling; topology_derived analysis of that construct also resolves to this same N-terminal junction, providing corroborating surface-validation evidence. Full-length Mertk construct (PMC11050108) with an IFN-γR2 signal peptide driving surface localization, a FLAG tag sequence, and a linker placed immediately N-terminal to the Mertk mature peptide (i.e., after the signal peptide cleavage site, before residue 21). Two independent papers (PMC4206827) additionally confirm that N-terminally HA-tagged mouse Mer (close ortholog) is detected on the cell surface by live-cell (non-permeabilized) labeling, corroborating tolerance of an N-terminal extracellular tag at this junction.

sources.claim: Preceding the Mertk insert is an interferon–γ receptor 2 signal peptide ( NM_005534.3 ) for surface localization, a FLAG tag sequence, and a linker sequence containing a Sal1 restriction site.

literature_notes: L3 and L4 (PMC4206827) describe HA-tagged recombinant mouse Mer confirmed on the cell surface by live-cell (non-permeabilized) labeling and inducible expression. Neither clip specifies the insertion residue or terminus. Because MERTK is a type I single-pass receptor with exactly one extracellular terminus (the mature N-terminus after SP cleavage), topology_derived reasoning resolves both clips to insert_after_residue=20, the same junction already validated by L1. They are therefore treated as corroborating evidence for the single L1-grounded site rather than separate sites at a distinct junction. L2 describes an Emerald GFP + Myc tag fused to the C-terminus of full-length Mertk; the C-terminus (residue 999) is intracellular (topology landmarks: intracellular 523–999) and is recorded in other_positions.

literature_other_positions.note: Emerald GFP and Myc tag fused after the C-terminus of full-length Mertk; residue 999 falls within the intracellular domain (landmarks: 523–999), so this is a cytoplasmic tag, not a surface tag.
